title: "Git and GitHub"

## Set up once

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Check that Git works | `git --version` |
| Your name and email, written into every commit | `git config --global user.name "NAME"` and `git config --global user.email "EMAIL"` |
| Call the first branch `main` | `git config --global init.defaultBranch main` |

See [lesson 04, section 1](../pages/04-git.qmd#is-git-set-up) and [lesson 00](../pages/00-setup.qmd#git-and-github) for the SSH key.

## Track changes

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Start tracking a project | `git init` |
| What changed, what is staged? | `git status` (one line per file: `git status --short`) |
| Why is a file not listed? | `git check-ignore -v FILE` |
| Show changes you have not staged | `git diff` |
| Stage one file, or everything | `git add FILE`, `git add .` |
| Record the staged changes | `git commit -m "MESSAGE"` |
| Stage and commit every changed tracked file | `git commit -am "MESSAGE"` (does not add new files) |
| Delete a file and stage the deletion | `git rm FILE` |

Taught in [lesson 04, sections 2 to 4](../pages/04-git.qmd#start-tracking-the-project).

## Look back

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| One line per commit | `git log --oneline` |
| The commits that changed one file | `git log --oneline -- FILE` |
| All branches as a graph | `git log --oneline --graph --all` |
| What the last commit changed | `git show --stat HEAD` |
| Get files back as they were one commit ago | `git restore --source=HEAD~1 FILE` |

See [section 5](../pages/04-git.qmd#browse-the-history) and the [*Break it*](../pages/04-git.qmd#break-it-delete-your-work-then-get-it-back).

## Branches

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Make a branch and switch to it | `git switch -c BRANCH` |
| Switch to another branch | `git switch main` |
| Merge a branch into the one you are on | `git merge BRANCH` |
| Delete a merged branch | `git branch -d BRANCH` |
| Finish a merge conflict | edit the files (remove the `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>` lines), then `git add FILE` and `git commit -m "MESSAGE"` |

See [sections 7 and 8](../pages/04-git.qmd#branches).

## GitHub

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Connect your project to a new GitHub repository | `git remote add origin git@github.com:USER/REPO.git` |
| Push a branch the first time | `git push -u origin BRANCH` |
| Push and pull later | `git push`, `git pull` |
| Copy a repository to your computer | `git clone git@github.com:USER/REPO.git FOLDER` |
| Pull request | push a branch, then *Compare & pull request* on GitHub; merge when the *Reproduce* check is green |

See [section 6](../pages/04-git.qmd#put-the-project-on-github) and [section 10](../pages/04-git.qmd#pull-requests-and-the-reproduce-check).

## Tags

| What you want | Command |
|------------|------------------------|
| Name the current commit | `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "MESSAGE"` |
| Push the tag to GitHub | `git push origin v1.0.0` |
| List tags | `git tag` |

See [section 9](../pages/04-git.qmd#tags); releases with a DOI are in [lesson 12](../pages/12-putting-it-together.qmd#release-and-archive-on-zenodo).

## `.gitignore`, as in the template

```{.gitignore}
# Environments: rebuilt from pixi.lock
.pixi/*
# Downloaded data, except its README
data/raw/**
!data/raw/README.md
# Rebuilt by code
results/**
reports/*.html
```

Commit what people write; ignore what programs download or rebuild. A `#`
starts a comment only at the beginning of a line.
